cases.name: the per-VM process mode: the daemon's VMs are jailed apz-vmm children (APZ_VMM_SPAWN=process)
cases.vector: a daemon started with APZ_VMM_SPAWN=process boots its 2-role fleet (noded --agents) as two apz-vmm children; the case reads the kernel's own view of each child: the parent linkage (/proc/<pid>/stat's PPid: a child count == the VM count), /proc/<pid>/mountinfo's `/` root = that child's own jail dir under the jail base (settled by inode identity with the host-side dir) with no /etc/hostname in /proc/<pid>/root while the host has one, Seccomp: 2 on every VMM thread of the child, the child's own stderr line 'parent-death signal armed (SIGKILL)' once per child, a /tell uptime on a real fleet agent (200, two numbers — the muxer path end to end), and the backstop: no apz-vmm child alive 10 s after the daemon is SIGKILLed

notes: the child's log is read here through the product's own APZ_VMM_CHILD switch (with an exec wrapper that tees the child's stderr), because the daemon captures that stream into VmRuntime::process_log and surfaces it nowhere: noded.log carries no child line, and GET /api/v0/runs/{id} returns a VM's serial, not its process log. Recorded as a finding.

cases.name: an API-created run in process mode: the VMs a POST booted are still up after the request
cases.vector: a daemon started with APZ_VMM_SPAWN=process boots a 2-VM run through POST /api/v0/runs; after a 3 s settle the run is still running, the daemon still has its 2 apz-vmm children, and the guests' console captures are non-empty — the request that created the VMs must not be able to take them down. FAILS on HEAD: apz-vmm arms PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) against the thread that spawned it (the HTTP request thread, which exits when the response is written)

findings.title: the per-VM process's own boot log — the jailer's root, the parent-death arming — is captured in memory and surfaced nowhere
findings.observed: the children's stderr carries the jailer's line and the arming line; noded.log carries neither, and no endpoint exposes VmRuntime::process_log (a run's VM rows carry serial only)
findings.expected: an operator can read the child's boot log for a VM (a log line or an API field)
findings.suspected_component: crates/noded (no log line for VmRuntime::process_log) + crates/vmm/src/spawner (VmHandle::process_log has no API)
